knowledge:
- key_parameters: esetm=Gene expression matrix (probes/genes as rows, samples as columns) ;; group=Vector of class labels (e.g., disease vs. control) ;; paired=Logical indicating if the experimental design is paired ;; block=Vector specifying blocks/pairs for paired designs ;; targetgs=Target gene sets expected to be relevant in the dataset, used for plotting and benchmarking ;; annotation=Annotation package name (e.g., "hgu133plus2.db") ;; gslist=Gene set list to analyze, e.g., "KEGGRESTpathway" ;; organism=Three-letter organism code, e.g., "hsa" ;; Nmin=Minimum number of genes in a gene set to be considered ;; NI=Number of permutations for significance evaluation (use 1000 for accurate results) ;; plots=Logical to generate diagnostic plots showing how gene weighting improves the analysis ;; parallel=Logical to run permutations in parallel (requires doParallel) ;; ncr=Number of cores to use when parallel=TRUE
- alternatives: ABSmT (PADOG without gene weights, represented by PmeanAbsT in the output) can be used but is generally inferior because it does not down-weight overlapping genes. GSA (Gene Set Analysis) is mentioned as an alternative reference method for benchmarking.
- when_to_use: Use PADOG when performing gene set or pathway analysis on gene expression data (such as microarray data) and you want to reduce the influence of ubiquitous/overlapping genes that appear in many pathways, thereby improving the specificity and ranking of truly relevant pathways.
- pitfalls: Using a low number of permutations (e.g., NI = 50) is useful for quick testing but insufficient for publication-quality p-values; NI = 1000 is recommended. Ensure the annotation package name is correctly formatted (e.g., appending ".db" to the annotation string). For benchmarking, custom methods must return a dataframe with exact columns (ID, P, Rank, Dataset, Method) and filter out gene sets smaller than minsize.

workflows.name: pathway_analysis_with_padog
workflows.intent: Run PADOG pathway analysis on a gene expression matrix with group labels.
workflows.stages: 1. Run padog with specified parameters (permutations, annotation, organism, parallel processing) to compute pathway scores and p-values.
workflows.code:
myr = padog(
    esetm = dlist$dat.m,
    group = dlist$ano$Group,
    paired = dlist$design == "Paired",
    block = dlist$ano$Block,
    targetgs = dlist$targetGeneSets,
    annotation = dlist$annotation,
    gslist = "KEGGRESTpathway",
    organism = "hsa",
    verbose = FALSE,
    Nmin = 3,
    NI = 50,
    plots = TRUE,
    dseed = 1
)

myr2 = padog(

    parallel = TRUE

workflows.name: benchmark_gene_set_analysis
workflows.intent: Compare a custom gene set analysis method against PADOG using benchmark datasets.
workflows.stages: 1. Define a custom method function that loads datasets, filters annotations using filteranot, and returns a formatted dataframe. 2. Run compPADOG to compare the custom method against PADOG on selected datasets.
workflows.code:
randFun = function(dseed, mname = "myRand") {
    #a helper function to pass additional variables to your method
    getdataaslist = getdataaslist
    return(function(set, mygslist, minsize) {#your method function
        set.seed(dseed)
        #this loads the dataset 
        data(list = set, package = "KEGGdzPathwaysGEO")
        #extract the required info using the function defined earlier 
        dlist = getdataaslist(set)
        #get rid of duplicates probesets per ENTREZ ID by keeping the probeset 
        #with smallest p-value (computed using limma) 
        aT1 = filteranot(esetm = dlist$dat.m, group = dlist$ano$Group, 
            paired = dlist$design == "Paired", block = dlist$ano$Block, 
            annotation = dlist$annotation)
        #create an output dataframe for this toy method with random gene set p-values
        mygslistSize = unlist(lapply(mygslist, function(x) {
            length(intersect(aT1$ENTREZID, x))
        }))
        res = data.frame(ID = names(mygslist), P = runif(length(mygslist)),
            Size = mygslistSize, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
        res$FDR = p.adjust(res$P,"fdr")
        #drop genesets with less than minsize genes in the current dataset 
        res = res[res$Size >= minsize,]
        #compute ranks
        res$Rank = rank(res$P) / dim(res)[1]*100
        #needed to compare ranks between methods; must be the same as given 
        #in mymethods argument "list(myRand="
        res$Method = mname 
        #needed because comparisons of ranks between methods is paired at dataset level
        res$Dataset = dlist$dataset
        #output only result for the targetGeneSets 
        #which are gene sets expected to be relevant in this dataset
        return(res[res$ID %in% dlist$targetGeneSets,])
        }
    )
}

randomF = randFun(1)

mysets = c("GSE9348","GSE8671","GSE1297")
out = compPADOG(datasets = mysets, existingMethods = c("PADOG"),
    mymethods = list(myRand = randomF), 
    gslist = "KEGGRESTpathway", Nmin = 3, NI = 40, plots = TRUE, 
    verbose=FALSE, parallel = TRUE, dseed = 1, pkgs = NULL)
